history: Romans had two ways to talk about cheese. Caseus was the cheese itself. Formaticus was cheese pressed in a forma, a mould. The Romance languages split here. French fromage and Italian formaggio come from the mould. Portuguese and Spanish kept caseus: queijo and queso. The Latin sound -se- followed by a vowel turned into -ij- in Portuguese, the same change that made beijo, ‘kiss’, out of Latin basium. And English? It borrowed caseus very early, through the Germanic languages, and it became cheese. So queijo and cheese are cousins, a Serra da Estrela and a cheddar from the same Latin word. Try queijo fresco, queijo da Serra or queijo de Azeitão.
historyEinfach: Queijo means ‘cheese’. It comes from Latin caseus. Spanish queso comes from the same word. English cheese too! French fromage and Italian formaggio come from another Latin word: forma, the mould for the cheese. Portugal has famous cheeses, like queijo da Serra.

elsewhere.text: The Germanic tribes learned cheese-making words from the Romans, so cheese is a Latin loan.
French named the cheese after its mould, not after the cheese.
